items.text: Among adults treated through the OPAT service from 2021 to 2025, what is the rate of line complications requiring unplanned hospital contact or premature removal per 1,000 catheter days, and how does it vary by line type, antibiotic, course length, agency team and living alone?
items.population: Adults with an OPAT episode through a PICC or midline, January 2021 to December 2025
items.intervention: Line type, antibiotic, course length, agency team and living arrangement (exposures)
items.outcome: Line complication requiring unplanned hospital contact or premature removal
items.time: From line insertion to end of therapy
items.setting: Hospital OPAT service and its home infusion agency

items.text: How do patients, carers and agency nurses from high- and low-complication groups explain how line problems start, are noticed and are escalated at home?
items.population: Patients, family carers and agency nurses sampled from the extremes of the cohort results
items.intervention: Experience of line care and escalation at home
items.outcome: Explanations of how problems start, are noticed and are escalated

finer: Feasible with existing records and about 60 fellow hours if the interviews are limited to about 30; interesting to infectious diseases, vascular access and the agency; novel locally; ethical with REB approval and consent for interviews; relevant because it decides the service's first action.
summary: One quantitative question and one qualitative question, linked by the sampling plan.
